title: What we learned w/Broncos today: -J.K. Dobbins practiced, participated in individual drills -Dobbins said Monday was simply a limited practice -C Michael Deiter carted off the practice field -Sean Payton: Broncos will be “fine” & “good” at center despite injuries -Nik Bonitto: No one can block Que Robinson when he sets his mind to it -Bonitto and Von Miller have communicated in touch over the past year -Pat Bryant has stood out to Bonitto: “He’s going to be a player for sure” -Greg Penner: “We want Bo here long term” -Penner: Burnham Yard still preferred site, “we really want to stay in Denver if we can” -Jaylen Waddle, Alex Forsyth, Michael Bandy, Caleb Lohner and Dasan McCullough DNP -Will wear throwbacks in Week 6 and Week 18 -Greg Penner: Team hasn’t thought about PSLs
summary:
What we learned w/Broncos today:

-J.K. Dobbins practiced, participated in individual drills

-Dobbins said Monday was simply a limited practice

-C Michael Deiter carted off the practice field

-Sean Payton: Broncos will be “fine” & “good” at center despite injuries

-Nik Bonitto: No one can block Que Robinson when he sets his mind to it

-Bonitto and Von Miller have communicated in touch over the past year

-Pat Bryant has stood out to Bonitto: “He’s going to be a player for sure”

-Greg Penner: “We want Bo here long term”

-Penner: Burnham Yard still preferred site, “we really want to stay in Denver if we can”

-Jaylen Waddle, Alex Forsyth, Michael Bandy, Caleb Lohner and Dasan McCullough DNP

-Will wear throwbacks in Week 6 and Week 18

-Greg Penner: Team hasn’t thought about PSLs

Nearly intercepted multiple passes over the middle in the red zone. McFadden has looked good all camp. Giants have better ILB depth than at any point in my 11 seasons on the beat. • Abdul Carter was extremely disruptive today. He can just take over at times. I was high on Carter at this time a year ago and I'm doubling down. Fully expecting a Year 2 breakout. • I was positioned near the defensive sideline and behind DC Dennard Wilson for much of practice. Wilson's energy and intensity is infectious. Jaxson Dart over-threw Isaiah Likely on a fourth-and-goal from the 9 on a skinny post. Dart and the offensive players appealed to the official for DPI but got no flag. The defense demanded an offensive pass interference call and there was outrage when there was no call. There were real NFL officials working the practice, so that added legitimacy to the calls.

full_text:
Covered most of the biggest practice moments earlier, but a few highlights that stand out as I review my notes:

• Micah McFadden was extremely active in coverage. Nearly intercepted multiple passes over the middle in the red zone. McFadden has looked good all camp. Giants have better ILB depth than at any point in my 11 seasons on the beat. 

• Abdul Carter was extremely disruptive today. He can just take over at times. I was high on Carter at this time a year ago and I'm doubling down. Fully expecting a Year 2 breakout. 

• I was positioned near the defensive sideline and behind DC Dennard Wilson for much of practice. Wilson's energy and intensity is infectious. 

Deonte Banks had a steady dialogue of trash talk throughout practice. Been a long time since he's played well enough to pull that off. His confidence is clearly rising. 

Jaxson Dart over-threw Isaiah Likely on a fourth-and-goal from the 9 on a skinny post. Dart and the offensive players appealed to the official for DPI but got no flag. The defensive sideline reveled in mocking Dart/the offense. 

The offense got the last laugh in the period with Dalen Cambre leaping to catch a TD pass from Jameis Winston on fourth-and-goal from the 4. The defense demanded an offensive pass interference call and there was outrage when there was no call. 

There were real NFL officials working the practice, so that added legitimacy to the calls.

title: Notes and observations from #49ers practice No. 11, a joint joint with the #Titans: - HC Kyle Shanahan took another step in his recovery today, shedding the cast on his left hand in favor of a black brace. - One more injury: Didn't catch which one it was but saw a member of the officiating crew being helped to the training room. Looked like perhaps an accidental collision with a player which led to a pronounced limp. 

- As a reminder, I only got to see bits and pieces of the Niners defense (see @TDavenport_NFL's timeline for highlights from over there) so much of this will be focused on the Niners offense. And I'll have some special teams notes at the end. 

- Well documented thing: this session started with A LOT of skirmishes of varying degrees. It was mostly on the other field where the Niners defense was agitating but there were a few close calls on the side for SF's offense as well. One thing that was repeatedly amusing: Any time a fight or near fight broke out near the Niners offense, OT Trent Williams would casually walk in and it would break up fairly quickly. The big fella commands a lot of respect. 

- It was a bit of a slow start for the offense, particularly in the run game. That could have been due to two things: 1. DT Jeffery Simmons, who remains awesome. 2. The lack of top running backs. The size and speed are obvious but there's a maturity and understanding of the game that his teammates and coaches continue to notice that are helping him adapt quickly. - Deebo is getting a lot of work in the back field and at receiver right now and set the tone in this practice a bit with his hard-charging style. His best play of the day: A tremendous one-handed, left-handed catch in the red zone on a ball Purdy threw behind him. Deebo also revved up the run game a bit as practice went on. 

- Jones and the second unit also had their share of success aside from the one interception (Jones tried to go back shoulder to Jordan Watkins but didn't get it out far enough to that shoulder and the defender jumped in front for the pick). Had Jones at 15-of-19 with particularly strong work in the red zone. In that sequence he found Deebo for a nice gain over the middle then followed with touchdown strikes to Stribling and TE Brayden Willis. The touch throw to Willis in the back of the end zone stood out. 

- Speaking of Willis, today was his turn to state a case for more of a role and a roster spot. Had him down for five grabs during team periods. Will be curious to see if he can carry it over to games. TE Jake Tonges also made his share of plays today. 

- Robert Jones continues to work at LG with the top offense with Willis with the 2s. Shanahan mentioned Willis as someone they want to see more of there as the season nears. Willis got flagged for a hold today but otherwise seemed to hold up well. If he can stay on the field, there seems to be a path to playing early. That's a ways off given the time he missed but it exists. 

- RB Khalil Herbert got the Niners fired up with a red zone run in which he lowered his shoulder, delivered a blow and kept rolling toward the end zone. McCaffrey hustled out to hype Herbert up after the play. 

- One random thing to like today: On a run play that resulted in Deebo getting the carry, RB Sincere McCormick was charged with acting as his lead blocker. McCormick got to his spot, delivered a well-timed block and opened the hole for a nice gain for Deebo. 

- To his credit after the fumble early, Turner bounced back late and made a pair of catches from Jones and drew a DPI penalty for Purdy in the final two-minute periods. 

- Some other Titans defensive notables: After an early completion from QB Mac Jones to WR Malik Turner, Titans CB Micah Robinson forced and recovered a fumble which fired up the Tennessee side. LB Cody Barton had a PBU on a throw from Purdy for WR De'Zhaun Stribling, Simmons got to Purdy for a pressure or would-be sack on a couple of occasions, DE Jermaine Johnson forced a Purdy throwaway, LB Anthony Hill nearly intercepted a pass from Jones for WR Jordan Watkins, DBs Mario Goodrich and Nazeeh Johnson came up with interceptions against Kurtis Rourke and Jones, respectively. 

- On the special teams front, it's hard to read too much into things right now but here's how the Niners did some things: Corliss Waitman was up first with the punt team with Jack Bouwmeester then getting his turn. Not sure there's much to read into it but we'll see how that goes in preseason games. 

In the return game, it was Watkins up first as the punt returner with work for Junior Bergen and Will Pauling, among others. 

- As you might expect, the field with the 49ers offense got done a handful of minutes before the other one. The fighting delayed the work being done there a bit. 

- Also as you might expect, Shanahan said there won't be many starters playing in the preseason game Thursday. Today serves a similar purpose so the backups will get most of those reps. 

- That's all for today. Thanks for reading.

Jordan van den Berg opened at DT with the 1st during the short-yardage goal line period. He continues to work his way into the rotation with the 1s. DB Anthony Johnson Jr. and LB Jon Rhattigan were also with the 1s at the goal line.

Did not see where Tyrique Stevenson went for the final period of practice. Malik Muhammad, who was with the 1s at nickel, moved outside to Stevenson's spot.

title: Eagles Training Camp Player of the Day, Day 10: Offensive Line The story of practice on Tuesday was the Eagles running game and dominating in that department started with the offensive line. At the end of practice the Eagles ran an 11v1 drill where the offense had to get a first-down to kill off the clock to ice away a win. It took the Eagles offense exactly two plays to get the job done with the offensive line creating openings big enough for Saquon Barkley to get through and get the first down. Through 10 practices I have been pretty encouraged by the running game and the offensive line. It can be hard to get a true read on the running game at times (no pads, no tackling, etc) but it seems they are adjusting well to the new scheme and are pretty consistently creating openings for the running backs. If the offense is going to be good this year it will require good offensive line play. So far in camp the teams seems to be on their way to getting just that.

full_text:
Eagles Training Camp Player of the Day, Day 10: Offensive Line

The story of practice on Tuesday was the Eagles running game and dominating in that department started with the offensive line. 

At the end of practice the Eagles ran an 11v1 drill where the offense had to get a first-down to kill off the clock to ice away a win. It took the Eagles offense exactly two plays to get the job done with the offensive line creating openings big enough for Saquon Barkley to get through and get the first down. 

Through 10 practices I have been pretty encouraged by the running game and the offensive line. It can be hard to get a true read on the running game at times (no pads, no tackling, etc) but it seems they are adjusting well to the new scheme and are pretty consistently creating openings for the running backs. 

If the offense is going to be good this year it will require good offensive line play. So far in camp the teams seems to be on their way to getting just that.

title: Fight AND practice highlights of that 49ers-Titans joint session.... 🏈 Brock Purdy was dominant facing a familiar Robert Saleh defense. 13 has been locked in all camp. Especially good in the red zone, where he found Deebo for multiple TDs and again connected with Luke Farrell (growing theme) 🏈Bullying vibe, especially early, from the 49ers defense. Tennessee took exception, hence the fights. A first-play Upton Stout shove and a second-play Dre Greenlaw/Fred Warner TFL on a pitch right set a very physical tone. Then, after Renardo Green leveled Carnell Tate, matters exploded 🏈Two Titans' O-linemen eventually ejected. Skirmish activity extended into back half of practice after 49ers DT Osa Odighizuwa sacked Cam Ward and grabbed his shoulder pad. Tennessee didn't like that 🏈Titans seemed to have some rushing success vs 49ers, though it's very hard to gauge without watching the tape. Ward's accuracy was very inconsistent. Lowlight for him was Ji'Ayir Brown's pick 6, which followed the Osa vs. Dan Moore Jr. Round II 🏈Big picture on 49ers offense: They'll need to be a top-5 unit this year, and Purdy has given every indication that he can guide that type of success from his QB spot. Layered passes, scrambles, elite RZ production... all there 🏈49ers vet DB Nate Hobbs was very active and physical for the 49ers today... seemed to be at the center of much of the action 🏈49ers safety Marques Sigle notched a couple PBUs 🏈Second-year corner Jakob Robinson logged a leaping INT against Titans QB Will Levis. It was intended for WR Mason Kinsev, who seemed to be doing a lot of today's jawing — including one session vs 49ers rookie safety Jalen Stroman 🏈I found Levis throwing a pick with Levi's Stadium in the background was funny 🏈One good red-zone rep for the 49ers involved rookie LBs Jaden Dugger and Larry Worth — nearly 14 feet of combined wingspan between them — flush Levis out of the pocket and force an incompletion. Was an imposing sight; Worth was FIRED UP 🏈Romello Height had some good, explosive work against Moore — a starting LT — that disrupted Ward. A lot of emotion in this one; Height was fired up on the sideline. Offsides flags still a concern 🏈Warner is a strategic instigator — talked quite a bit in Ward's direction in between series🍿. Also a good face-to-face confrontation with the much shorter RB Tyjae Spears 🏈Raheem Morris blitzed Warner numerous times today. The most I can remember Warner being asked to go straight after the QB. Another data point in evaluating this evolving 49ers' defense 🏈Former Stanford WR Elic Ayomanor had some good battles vs 49ers CBs Renardo Green (great coverage on a deep ball) and Jack Jones. Ayomanor beat Jones on a double move but Jones recovered for a last-second PBU 🏈Next up: Preseason opener vs these same Titans. Robert Saleh said Tennessee will play everyone and Kyle Shanahan said the 49ers will sit most starters. All in all, coaches happy with the productive work today. Good eval opportunity for the 49ers coming up in an actual game environment...

title: MIke LaFleur was pressed today on why Josh Sweat, who's still on the PUP list, hasn't practice at all during training camp. “Still going through his process of making sure that Josh Sweat is where he needs to be and how he feels where he needs to be to be at his best," LaFleur said. "So, progressing good. I know what Monti said to you. My message isn't any different. He's in a good spot right now, but we just need a little bit more time." But then LaFleur was asked if it's been a three-week ramp-up to get Sweat ready for the season. "Yeah. I mean, there's different parts of injuries and stuff like that that, you know, are...and I shouldn't even call it injuries...but just getting himself right to be ready to roll. So, again, I like where he's at. I know everyone probably is not believing me on that one, but again, I only try to speak truth to you guys." LaFleur said the decision for Sweat not to practice is a "collective" decision, including non-team opinions.

title: With today being the last day of training in Glendale for the Cardinals, coach Mike LaFleur said he "absolutely" got done what he wanted to at State Farm Stadium over the last 20 days. "We took it one day at a time, one block at a time, and I thought there was improvement, but still a long way to go," he said. LaFleur on his main takeaways from training camp: "That they are where their feet are, that they come to work every single day, that they want to improve. Again, I thought our operation was good, got a long way to go. I thought our play style was good, got a long way to go. And then they also know that we have a long way to go once that ball snapped in terms of details, fundamentals, all those kind of things within our schemes. So, again, I was pleased with the work that we put in within that time, but long way to go."

Rookie RG Sisi Mauigoa didn’t do team work after looking like he twisted his ankle Monday and received some sort of upper body exam. Daniel Faalele stepped into his spot. Aaron Stinnie saw some reps there, too 

CB Paulson Adebo wasn’t out here at all. Neither were WRs JuJu Smith-Schuster (2nd straight day) and Jalin Hyatt or center John Michael Schmitz and Lucas Patrick

CBs Greg Newsome and Dru Phillips continued to work on the side

Rookie CB Colton Hood saw 1st team defense work for a second straight day. WR Braxton Berrios earned some 1st team offense opps

TE Thomas Fidone has become one of the ‘big play a day’ guys on the roster. Made a great one-handed catch from Jameis Winston going up the seam today

Malik Nabers again did individual work @NYDailyNews #TalkinBall

He had some really high completion days where he was able to show some really, really good understanding of just putting the ball in play, playing with great timing, rhythm. You guys have seen him be explosive when there's opportunities there, but you've also seen him check the ball down and put the ball in play and get us from a 1st and 10 to a 2nd and 3. And then, as you continued to look at the body of work through those ten days, what jumped out is what could be."

No one stopped the pass rush -Nice run by Tyjae Spears. Slow to the hole, exploded through made a nice cut back at the 2nd level and ran away from the defense -Ridley sighting. Diving catch on speed out vs Deommodre Lenoir -Enter the Sandman came on. Michael Carter delivered a couple physical run w/Jackson Slater at center. Andre James at RG -Levis at QB tried to find Hank Beatty on out-breaking rte. Jakob Robinson dove in front of it for the INT -Punt team. Mason Kinsey good job getting down there but stayed too close to the returner and drew a flag -Tommy Townsend boomed his 4th punt. Made the returner go back and catch it Willie Mays style (SF Giants reference😉)
summary:
#Titans #49ers joint practice notes (2)
-Levis up. A couple of hand offs to Michael Carter then a boot pass to Jaran Kanak for a 1st. Kanak got blasted but held on to it
-Ward behind Tate across the middle
-Daniel Bellinger w/the pancake on former Titans OLB Sam Okuayinonu. JC Latham got him a couple plays later but Ward to Ridley fell incomplete
-Cody Barton good instincts dropping into pass lane and skied up to knock down a pass intended for De'Zhaun Stribbling
-Trubisky just got surrounded by 49ers DLine. No one stopped the pass rush
-Nice run by Tyjae Spears. Slow to the hole, exploded through made a nice cut back at the 2nd level and ran away from the defense
-Ridley sighting. Diving catch on speed out vs Deommodre Lenoir
-Enter the Sandman came on. Michael Carter delivered a couple physical run w/Jackson Slater at center. Andre James at RG
-Levis at QB tried to find Hank Beatty on out-breaking rte. Jakob Robinson dove in front of it for the INT
-Punt team. Mason Kinsey good job getting down there but stayed too close to the returner and drew a flag
-Tommy Townsend boomed his 4th punt. Made the returner go back and catch it Willie Mays style (SF Giants reference😉)

#Titans #49ers joint practice notes (2)

-Ward behind Tate across the middle
-Daniel Bellinger w/the pancake on former Titans OLB Sam Okuayinonu. JC Latham got him a couple plays later but Ward to Ridley fell incomplete
-Cody Barton good instincts dropping into pass lane and skied up to knock down a pass intended for De'Zhaun Stribbling
-Trubisky just got surrounded by 49ers DLine. No one stopped the pass rush
-Nice run by Tyjae Spears. Slow to the hole, exploded through made a nice cut back at the 2nd level and ran away from the defense
